variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
x = 10

-- With type signature
y :: Int
y = 20
variables.notes: Variables in Haskell are immutable. Once bound to a value, they cannot be changed. Pattern matching is often used in bindings.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
a :: Int = 42
b :: Integer = 9999999999999999
c :: Float = 3.14
d :: Double = 2.71828
e :: Bool = True
f :: Char = 'X'
g :: String = "Hello"

-- Algebraic Data Type
data Shape = Circle Float | Rectangle Float Float
data_types.notes: Haskell is statically typed with strong type inference. You can define custom Algebraic Data Types (ADTs).

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
add = 5 + 3
sub = 5 - 3
mul = 5 * 3
divFloat = 5.0 / 2.0
divInt = 5 `div` 2
remInt = 5 `mod` 2

andBool = True && False
orBool = True || False
notBool = not True

eq = 5 == 5
neq = 5 /= 3
operators.notes: Operators are just functions. Backticks allow using any binary function as an infix operator (e.g., `div`).

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
result = if x > 0 
         then "Positive" 
         else "Non-positive"

-- Using guards (more common in functions)
sign x
  | x > 0     = 1
  | x < 0     = -1
  | otherwise = 0
conditionals.notes: if-then-else is an expression, so it must always have an 'else' branch and both branches must return the same type. Guards are often preferred for multiple conditions.

for_loop.title: For Loop (Mapping)
for_loop.code:
-- Applying a function to each element (map)
squares = map (\x -> x * x) [1..5]
-- Result: [1, 4, 9, 16, 25]

-- Using list comprehensions
evens = [x * 2 | x <- [1..5]]
for_loop.notes: Haskell has no traditional 'for' loop. Iteration is typically done using higher-order functions like map, fold, or list comprehensions.

while_loop.title: While Loop (Recursion)
while_loop.code:
-- Recursion to simulate while loop
countdown :: Int -> IO ()
countdown 0 = putStrLn "Liftoff!"
countdown n = do
  print n
  countdown (n - 1)
while_loop.notes: Haskell has no 'while' loop. State changes over time are modeled using recursion or monadic constructs.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
add :: Int -> Int -> Int
add x y = x + y

-- Lambda expression
multiply = \x y -> x * y

-- Pattern matching
factorial 0 = 1
factorial n = n * factorial (n - 1)
functions.notes: Functions are first-class and curried by default. Pattern matching is extensively used for flow control.

arrays.title: Arrays (Lists)
arrays.code:
numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

-- Cons operator to prepend
newNumbers = 0 : numbers

-- Concatenation
combined = [1, 2] ++ [3, 4]

-- Indexing (0-based, O(n))
third = numbers !! 2
arrays.notes: Lists are homogeneous linked lists, widely used in Haskell. For O(1) random access, use Data.Array or Data.Vector.

maps.title: Maps (Dictionaries)
maps.code:
import qualified Data.Map as Map

myMap = Map.fromList [("apple", 1), ("banana", 2)]

-- Insert
newMap = Map.insert "cherry" 3 myMap

-- Lookup
val = Map.lookup "apple" myMap -- Returns Just 1
maps.notes: Data.Map provides a balanced binary tree implementation. It is immutable, so updates return a new map.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
-- Using Maybe for possible failure
safeDivide :: Int -> Int -> Maybe Int
safeDivide _ 0 = Nothing
safeDivide x y = Just (x `div` y)

-- Using Either for detailed errors
divideOrError :: Int -> Int -> Either String Int
divideOrError _ 0 = Left "Division by zero"
divideOrError x y = Right (x `div` y)
error_handling.notes: Haskell uses ADTs like Maybe and Either for safe error handling instead of exceptions, forcing the caller to handle failures.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
-- Single-line comment
{- Multi-line
   comment block -}
add :: Int -> Int -> Int
add a b = a + b
comments.notes: Haskell uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.code:
x = 42 :: Int
big = 100000000000000000000 :: Integer
piVal = 3.14159 :: Double
hexVal = 0xFF
numbers.notes: Haskell supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.code:
isActive = True
isDone = False
result = isActive && not isDone
booleans.notes: Haskell treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.code:
intVal = 42 :: Int
floatVal = fromIntegral intVal :: Double
strVal = show intVal
parsed = read "123" :: Int
type_casting.notes: Haskell performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.notes: Haskell represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.code:
import Text.Printf
msg = printf "User %s scored %d" "Alice" (95 :: Int)
string_formatting.notes: Haskell formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.code:
describeList xs = case xs of
    []       -> "Empty list"
    [x]      -> "Single element"
    (x:y:_)  -> "Multiple elements"
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Haskell, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.code:
-- Infinite lazy sequence
evens = [0, 2 .. 20]
-- List slice with take/drop
sub = take 5 (drop 2 [1..10])
range.notes: Haskell constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.code:
-- List comprehension
squares = [x * x | x <- [1..10], even x]
iterators.notes: Haskell achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.notes: Haskell emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.code:
list = [1, 2, 3]
appended = 0 : list  -- Cons: O(1)
merged = list ++ [4, 5] -- Concat
lists.notes: Lists in Haskell are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Haskell uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.code:
import qualified Data.Set as Set
s = Set.fromList [1, 2, 3]
s' = Set.insert 4 s
exists = Set.member 2 s'
sets.notes: Haskell provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.notes: Haskell isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
